title: Chapter 218: Different From What I Thought
html:
“That simple?” Han Qiuming and Tian Teng’s employees exchanged disbelieving looks. The tape recorder was large; finding it should be easy.

“You’re serious?” Ye Xiaoxin opened her notebook. Despite reviewing dozens of Haunted Houses, she had never encountered a challenge like this.

“The recorder belongs to Tian Teng Medical School, so consider this an opportunity to reclaim it.” Chen Ge locked their waivers in a cabinet, suspecting he might need them soon.

“You’ve given up so early?” Han Qiuming seemed to be rather disappointed.

“This way.” Ignoring him, Chen Ge led the group into Night of the Living Dead.

“These props date from the beginning of the century and haven’t been maintained in months. The mannequins look handmade by children, everything is piled together, and there’s no coherent story. You expect us to experience this? Are you insulting us?” Han Qiuming spoke viciously, but his talent was genuine; one glance had exposed Night of the Living Dead’s every weakness.

Even Ye Xiaoxin and Su Luoluo found the scenario underwhelming. Still listing its flaws, Han Qiuming started forward, only for Guo Miao to stop him.

“Old Guo, why are you stopping me?” Guo Miao shook his head, heart racing beneath a deep sense of foreboding. “Something about the atmosphere is wrong.”

“What is so weird about it?”

“I can’t explain it, but this doesn’t feel like an ordinary room.” Guo Miao drew a cold breath. “I felt the same way while inspecting the hospital where Xu Zhenzhen’s incident occurred. It was broad daylight, yet panic overwhelmed me. I fled after five minutes.”

“Stop frightening yourself.” Han Qiuming shook off his hand and entered Night of the Living Dead.

“I abandoned this scenario some time ago but haven’t yet removed it.” Looking at Han Qiuming reminded Chen Ge of Fei Youliang. After this visit, perhaps Fei Youliang would no longer be lonely in the hospital.

Chen Ge lifted the wooden panel, releasing a surge of cold air. He surveyed the visitors and pointed down the black staircase. “The Third Sick Hall is below.”

“Underground?”

The visitors gathered around the opening. The stairs seemed to descend into endless darkness. Unfinished exam papers littered the charred steps, while a faint stench seeded dreadful possibilities in their minds.

“The left corridor leads to Mu Yang High School; the right leads to the Third Sick Hall. The scenarios connect, so choose carefully.” Chen Ge offered one final warning. “Both are enormous. Stay together.”

Chen Ge took out his phone. “Bring me the recorder within twenty minutes, and the game ends.”

No one moved until an unseen hand pushed Han Qiuming from behind, sending him stumbling forward.

“The clock is running.” At Chen Ge’s urging, they descended. As the last visitor vanished into darkness, he raised the wooden panel and waved. “Have fun.”

After sealing the entrance, Chen Ge returned to the control room and confronted a difficult choice of music. He rarely played Wedding Dress or Black Friday for ordinary visitors, using them only as occasional hidden surprises.

“Han Qiuming identified Night of the Living Dead’s weaknesses at a glance, so he has more than arrogance. Tian Teng’s actors are accustomed to Haunted House atmospheres, and ordinary scares won’t affect them. Ye Xiaoxin is a professional reviewer with exceptional nerves. Su Luoluo is the only innocent victim Guo Miao dragged into this.”

Treating professionals too gently would be disrespectful. Hand on the mouse, Chen Ge hesitated between two tracks. “Which is more suitable? Only children choose. We’re all adults here.”

He queued both songs, then entered the dressing room and donned Doctor Skull-cracker’s costume and makeup. “They won’t realize the face beneath the mask is worse, will they?”

Chen Ge packed everything and entered the Third Sick Hall with the faceless nurse’s uniform.

…

The wooden panel closed, sealing away the outside world’s warmth and hope. Du Chaojin, the youngest, shuddered. Ten seconds inside was enough to inspire regret. He should never have agreed so readily. I should have followed Sister Rui and Brother Lin. I’m too young for this.

A cold draft with no apparent source sent exam papers fluttering along the left corridor. Shadows shifted inside the classrooms as though watching. The group remained motionless for a full minute before Guo Miao finally spoke. “Mr. Han, you’re the most experienced. We’re relying on you.”

Han Qiuming adjusted his glasses. He had studied everything since entering. In atmosphere and environmental detail alone, Western Jiujiang’s House of Horrors surpassed most attractions he had visited. “No wonder he calls it Jiujiang’s scariest Haunted House. Interesting.”

Mannequins crowded the far end of the left corridor, some standing, others sprawled across the floor. The visitors stared at them and felt the unmistakable sensation of being watched in return.

“Boss, did that mannequin’s head move?” Song An grabbed Guo Miao’s arm.

“No.” Guo Miao had also gone pale. “But I think the schoolgirl in the middle just smiled at me.”

“I saw that, too. Wait, did she just move? Why is she suddenly closer to us?”

“It must be an illusion…”

“Are you finished?” Han Qiuming moved ahead. “The more frightening the left scenario appears, the better our position. You should thank me.”

“Why?” Xiao Du hid in the rear, already considering surrender.

“Boss Chen tried to deceive us. The left scenario is clearly his centerpiece, so it must be the hardest. Fortunately, I saw through him.” Han Qiuming approached the hospital door on the right and gripped its handle. “Without me, we would be inside the left scenario.”

“He has a point,” Xiao Du concurred meekly.

Song An nodded too. “The left side looks terrible. Thank goodness we chose the right. Well done, Mr. Han.”

They gathered in the right corridor. Only Guo Miao remained uneasy. “Boss Chen never struck me as a liar.”

“We’ll know when we see what is behind this door.”

Han Qiuming pulled open the Third Sick Hall’s door. Rusted hinges groaned, and the pungent smell of antiseptic struck them. Scratches and bloody messages scarred the old walls. From the hospital’s depths came faint, almost imperceptible screams.

Worst of all, countless figures wrapped in mattresses littered the dark corridor, transforming it into an open grave.

“This…”

Their limbs numbed as cold climbed from the soles of their feet to their scalps.
